newsitem.title: SAUDI ARABIA: Saudi Arabia launches three industrial projects.
newsitem.headline: Saudi Arabia launches three industrial projects.

text.p: Saudi Defence Minister Prince Sultan on Thursday opened three industrial projects in eastern Saudi Arabia worth more than seven billion riyals ($1.9 billion).
The minister laid the foundation stone for a new steel plant at the Saudi Iron and Steel Company, to be known as Hadeed. A flat steel plant and a new direct reduction facility will be built.
Hadeed is owned by Saudi Basic Industries Corp .
Voest-Alpine Industrieanlagenbau (VAI), a unit of Austria's VA Technologie, and Germany's SMS Schloemann Siemag AG, a unit of MAN AG, won SABIC's contract to build the steel plant.
VAI President and Chief Executive Officer Horst Wiesinger said the steel plant project, worth $880 million, would come on stream at the end of the third quarter of 1998.

Davy International, a unit of Trafalgar House, part of Norwegian technology and engineering group Kvaerner A/S, was awarded a $165 million contract to build the 1.1 million tonnes per year direct reduction plant last year.
Saudi Industry and Electricity Minister Hashem bin Abdullah bin Hashem Yamani described Hadeed as "the biggest iron and steel plant in the region".
Prince Sultan also inaugurated an MTBE (methyl tertiary butyl ether) project that would produce 700,000 tonnes a year for the Saudi Petrochemical Co (SADAF).
Yamani said investment in the project stood at 3.75 billion riyals, adding the plant would raise Saudi production of the gasoline additive to four million tonnes from a previous 2.7 million tonnes.
Formed in 1980, SADAF is a 50-50 joint venture between SABIC and Pecten Arabia Co, a unit of Shell Oil Co of the United States, itself an affiliate of Royal/Dutch Shell Group.
Officials said the new plant would be producing at full capacity next week.

Sultan also inaugurated the $150 million Gulf Ferroalloys Company (Sabayek), which is designed to produce 75,000 tonnes of metallic alloys a year. It is the first of its kind in the region. Production started earlier this year.

United Gulf Industries Corp (UGIC), publicly traded in Bahrain, owns a 26 percent stake in Sabayek and SABIC owns 15 percent. Austria's Decometal Aussenhandelsgesellschaft holds a seven percent stake and the rest is owned by financial institutions and Arab investors. ($1=3.75 riyals)
